Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: Comprehensive district-wide inventory including all schools with detailed site assessments, building ages, sizes, and specialized spaces. Robust condition assessment covers HVAC, roofing, plumbing, electrical, lighting, technology infrastructure, and accessibility, with connections to student outcomes and long-term capital planning (Chunks 1, 3, 13-16).

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: Detailed enrollment projections over a long-term horizon with methodology explained, including demographic trends, birth rates, transfers, and residential development. Capacity utilization data by site and classroom with surplus analysis and explicit connection to facility actions and consolidation strategies (Chunks 6-13).

Educational Alignment.justification: Educational alignment is a core organizing principle with clear integration of district mission, instructional priorities, and facilities planning. Detailed plans for academy-style learning environments at middle schools, technology integration, and program-specific facility upgrades (e.g., science labs, technology classrooms) directly linked to educational goals (Chunks 3, 15, 24-25).

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: Outdoor spaces are described mainly as playgrounds, fields, and amphitheaters with some mention of drainage and safety improvements. Limited detail on greening strategies, shade, or district-wide analysis of green space or climate resilience related to outdoor areas (Chunks 16-19).

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: Acknowledges energy efficiency and some energy management improvements but lacks detailed climate risk assessment or comprehensive climate resilience strategies. No explicit discussion of multiple climate impacts or district-wide climate readiness as a central theme (Chunks 3, 23).

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: Includes energy efficiency strategies such as window upgrades, HVAC improvements, roofing replacements with high-efficiency materials, and energy management systems. References state goals indirectly and discusses utility cost savings but lacks comprehensive energy resilience strategies like microgrids or full electrification plans (Chunks 3, 23-24).

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: Presents a detailed capital strategy with phased bond sales totaling over $30 million, detailed cost estimates including escalation and contingencies, clear prioritization of projects, and multiple funding sources. Includes long-term financial sustainability considerations and alignment with district priorities (Chunks 23-29).
